stories.title: From Abram to Bethlehem
stories.summary: A walk through passages from Genesis 12, the book of Ruth and Matthew 1–2, each linked to the one before it by the wording of the text.

steps.phrase: Get thee out of thy country
steps.note: Genesis 12 begins with these words to Abram.

steps.phrase: there was a famine in the land

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: there was a famine in the land
steps.note: The book of Ruth opens with the same words.

why.text: An existing connection links Genesis 12:10 and Ruth 1:1.

steps.phrase: the name of the other Ruth

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: So Boaz took Ruth

why.text: The word Ruth stands in both Ruth 1:4 and Ruth 4:13.

steps.phrase: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse

why.text: The word Jesse stands in both Ruth 4:17 and Matthew 1:5.

steps.phrase: Jesse begat David the king

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea

why.text: The word Jesus stands in both Matthew 1:16 and Matthew 2:1.

steps.phrase: And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda

why.text: The word Bethlehem stands in both Matthew 2:1 and Matthew 2:6.

steps.phrase: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah

why.text: An existing connection links Matthew 2:6 and Micah 5:2.

stories.title: Matthew 1–2: “by the prophet”
stories.summary: The places in Matthew 1–2 where the text says a word was spoken or written by a prophet, each followed by the passage it is linked to.

steps.phrase: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet
Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son

why.text: An existing connection links Matthew 1:22 and Isaiah 7:14.

steps.phrase: thus it is written by the prophet

why.text: The word prophet stands in both Matthew 1:22 and Matthew 2:5.

steps.phrase: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel

why.text: An existing connection links Matthew 2:5 and Micah 5:2.

steps.phrase: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet

why.text: The word prophet stands in both Matthew 2:5 and Matthew 2:15.

steps.phrase: called my son out of Egypt

why.text: An existing connection links Matthew 2:15 and Hosea 11:1.

steps.phrase: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet

why.text: The word prophet stands in both Matthew 2:15 and Matthew 2:17.

steps.phrase: A voice was heard in Ramah

why.text: An existing connection links Matthew 2:17 and Jeremiah 31:15.

steps.phrase: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets
steps.note: Here the text says “the prophets” and names no passage; this edition does not assign one.

why.text: The word spoken stands in both Matthew 2:17 and Matthew 2:23.

stories.title: From the beginning to Haran
stories.summary: A line through Genesis 1–12, following the words the chapters share: created, generations, and the names in the lists.

steps.phrase: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
So God created man in his own image

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: This is the book of the generations of Adam

why.text: The word created stands in both Genesis 1:27 and Genesis 5:1.

steps.phrase: Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: These are the generations of Shem

why.text: The word Shem stands in both Genesis 5:32 and Genesis 11:10.

steps.phrase: begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran

why.text: Later in the same chapter.

steps.phrase: they came unto Haran, and dwelt there

why.text: The word Abram stands in both Genesis 11:26 and Genesis 11:31.

steps.phrase: So Abram departed

why.text: The word Haran stands in both Genesis 11:31 and Genesis 12:4.
